To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relative weight of each attribute is not constant, but varies across types of social housing beneficiaries; that the relative weight varies across attributes; that the willingness to pay for the attributes also varies across the five types of social dwellers, and that the attributes that are valued more highly are those related to the quality and location of the dwellings.

(1) the attributes that are most important to the different types of social housing beneficiaries are: location, dwelling quality and size, and the quality of social services; (2) the willingness to pay for each of these attributes is different for the different types of beneficiaries, and is also different for the different attributes; and (3) the relative importance of each of these attributes varies according to whether the beneficiary is a current or potential social housing dweller, and also according to the dwelling type that
the most relevant attributes for social housing dwellers are the location of the house (and its surroundings), the quality and size of the house, and its price (or the amount of the subsidy).

the relative weight and subjective valuation of the attributes of social housing, and it is based on a stated-preference approach, which allows us to determine the willingness to pay for each such attribute, and thus to estimate the total value of the social housing programmes in the country.
